payload.concept_name: Does partial resampling decouple a random walk?
payload.claim: The paper's organizing question — whether (w_n, w_n^ρ) becomes independent under per-step resampling probability ρ — is exactly the decoupling-under-noise question, answered negatively (stability) here.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.5802/ahl.273|question|which groups resist noise-induced decoupling?|does partial resampling decouple a random walk?

payload.concept_name: Which groups resist noise-induced decoupling?
parent_path: Does partial resampling decouple a random walk?
payload.claim: The paper advances the open classification of which infinite groups are noise-sensitive vs. stable by establishing noise stability for non-elementary hyperbolic groups with infinite abelianization.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.5802/ahl.273|question|do perturbed trajectories shrink in boundary dimension?|does partial resampling decouple a random walk?

payload.concept_name: Do perturbed trajectories shrink in boundary dimension?
parent_path: Does partial resampling decouple a random walk?
payload.claim: From the proven mutual singularity, the authors explicitly raise whether dim ν_{π^ρ} < dim ν_{μ⊗μ} for all ρ<1, posing the dimension-shrinkage question.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.3842/sigma.2026.046|action|recast a problem as a solved one|

payload.concept_name: Recast a problem as a solved one
payload.claim: Proves the Capparelli–Meurman–Primc–Primc conjectures by showing their k=1 generating functions are slight variants of the Andrews-Gordon/Bressoud sum sides, so the conjecture inherits the known sum-to-product identity.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.3842/sigma.2026.046|action|recover known results as special cases|pressure-test your own result

payload.concept_name: Recover known results as special cases
payload.claim: Setting z=1 in the bivariate P_i(z,q) reproduces the established Andrews-Gordon product (Theorem 2), confirming the new result specializes to the known one.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.3842/sigma.2026.046|value|drawn to explicit construction|

payload.concept_name: Drawn to explicit construction
payload.claim: The proof builds explicit functional equations and concrete case-by-case 'flipping' arguments on frequency arrays rather than invoking an abstract representation-theoretic mechanism.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.3842/sigma.2026.046|value|parsimonious|

payload.concept_name: Parsimonious
payload.claim: The entire result turns on a single minimal change (x^{N} to z^{n}) and one argument covering both odd and even companion cases.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.3842/sigma.2026.046|action|prove several cases with one argument|

payload.concept_name: Prove several cases with one argument
payload.claim: The author proves the odd-row and even-row companion conjectures simultaneously with the same functional-equation system, unlike the prior single-case crystal proof.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.3842/sigma.2026.046|tool|bivariate generating function|

payload.concept_name: Bivariate generating function
payload.claim: P_i(z,q) = sum F(i,j,n) z^j q^n simultaneously tracks partition size and part count, the object whose multisum form is matched against known identities.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.3842/sigma.2026.046|question|can a small change of variable link a new identity to a solved one?|

payload.concept_name: Can a small change of variable link a new identity to a solved one?
payload.claim: The paper frames its gap as whether the conjectured identities are minor reparametrizations of Andrews-Gordon/Bressoud reachable by a single substitution.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115255|value|drawn to generalization|

payload.concept_name: Drawn to generalization
payload.claim: Generalizes Seymour's two-family incomparability theorem to arbitrarily long d-exceeding sequences of families.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115255|value|drawn to explicit construction|

payload.concept_name: Drawn to explicit construction
payload.claim: Establishes the existence of long d-exceeding sequences by explicitly cyclically reusing d+1 pairwise incomparable families.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115255|action|carry an established framework into a harder setting|

payload.concept_name: Carry an established framework into a harder setting
payload.claim: Carries Seymour's incomparable-families bound into the harder regime of long acyclic d-exceeding sequences.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115255|action|pin down the fundamental limit|

payload.concept_name: Pin down the fundamental limit
payload.claim: Locates the maximum d for arbitrarily long d-exceeding set sequences between (1-o(1))(1/e)2^k and (1/2)2^k - 2.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115255|action|construct a worst-case instance|pin down the fundamental limit

payload.concept_name: Construct a worst-case instance
payload.claim: Builds explicit arbitrarily-long sequences by cyclic reuse, realizing the lower bound on the limit.

payload.concept_name: Relax a symmetric constraint into a directional one
parent_path: Loosen a concept to cover the exceptions
payload.claim: Replaces pairwise (cyclic) incomparability with the acyclic d-exceeding condition indexed by j-i in [d].

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115255|question|what survives when structure is taken away?|

payload.concept_name: What survives when structure is taken away?
payload.claim: Shows the (1/4)2^k maximum survives the relaxation of incomparability to a sufficiently long 1-exceeding sequence.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2026.115255|question|does relaxing a constraint enlarge its extremum?|what survives when structure is taken away?

payload.concept_name: Does relaxing a constraint enlarge its extremum?
parent_path: What survives when structure is taken away?
payload.claim: Tests whether the acyclic relaxation admits larger equal-sized families, finding the same bound for 1-exceeding sequences.
